questions.stem: Jorund Pell sells 500 shares of a listed company on the TSX. The buyer is another ordinary investor, and Jorund is not a control person. How does the prospectus requirement apply?

options.A: It does not apply, because this trade is not a distribution
options.B: It applies, because every sale of listed shares is a distribution
options.C: It applies, unless Jorund first files a preliminary prospectus
options.D: It applies, because the shares were previously issued

questions.rationale: A distribution is a trade in securities not previously issued, or in previously issued securities from a control person's holdings. Ordinary exchange trading between investors is neither kind. Previously issued shares need a prospectus only when they come from a control person.
questions.source_quote: "a trade in previously issued securities of an issuer from the holdings of any control person," — research/sources/gov/ontario-securities-act-extracts.txt Securities Act (Ontario) s.1(1) 'distribution' (c), ~L102

questions.stem: Securities law requires a final prospectus to contain full, true and plain disclosure of all material facts. What is the main purpose of this requirement?

options.A: To guarantee that investors earn a return on the securities
options.B: To give investors all the important facts before they decide to invest
options.C: To replace the dealer's duty to assess suitability for each client
options.D: To protect the issuer from liability for statements in the prospectus

questions.rationale: The prospectus gives investors all the material facts before they decide. It guarantees no return. Statutory liability gives investors a remedy for poor disclosure, so the requirement does not protect the issuer. The dealer must still assess suitability.
questions.source_quote: "the statutory requirement that the final prospectus contain full, true and plain disclosure of all material facts" — research/sources/csa/cp-41-101-general-prospectus-requirements-companion-policy.txt 41-101CP s.6.12(7), ~L2637-2639

questions.stem: Halvard Instruments Inc. files a prospectus. It does not state that its largest customer, with 40% of its sales, has just cancelled its contract. How does securities law treat this omission?

options.A: It is acceptable, because the prospectus states only true facts
options.B: It is acceptable if the issuer discloses the loss in its next annual report
options.C: It is a misrepresentation, because it omits a material fact
options.D: It is a misrepresentation only if the issuer intended to mislead investors

questions.rationale: A material fact would reasonably be expected to have a significant effect on market price or value. Loss of 40% of sales is material. A misrepresentation includes an omission of a material fact that must be stated. The definition does not depend on intent.
questions.source_quote: "an untrue statement of material fact, or (b) an omission to state a material fact that is required to be stated or that is necessary to make a statement not misleading in the light of the circumstances in which it was made" — research/sources/gov/ontario-securities-act-extracts.txt Securities Act (Ontario) s.1(1) 'misrepresentation', ~L177-179

questions.stem: A regulator reviews the final prospectus of Quillon Energy Corp. Which reason allows the regulator to refuse a receipt?

options.A: Issuance of the receipt is not in the public interest
options.B: The underwriter has not yet found buyers for all of the shares
options.C: The issuer has never been a reporting issuer in Canada
options.D: The issuer filed a preliminary prospectus before the final one

questions.rationale: Securities legislation lets the regulator refuse a receipt where issuing it is not in the public interest. An IPO issuer is usually not yet a reporting issuer. A preliminary prospectus always comes first. No sale can occur before the final receipt, so unsold shares are normal.
questions.source_quote: "Securities legislation provides the regulator with discretion to refuse a receipt for a prospectus where it is not in the public interest to issue the receipt." — research/sources/csa/cp-41-101-general-prospectus-requirements-companion-policy.txt 41-101CP s.2.6(1), ~L549

questions.stem: Before Tamsin Biotech Inc. files a preliminary prospectus for its IPO, its CEO tells a podcast audience to buy shares in the coming offering. No exemption applies. How do securities rules treat the statement?

options.A: It is allowed, because the issuer has not yet sold any shares
options.B: It is allowed, because a podcast is not a written advertisement
options.C: It is a trade in furtherance of a distribution, so it breaches the prospectus requirement
options.D: It is allowed if the CEO later repeats the statement in the prospectus

questions.rationale: A trade includes any advertisement or conduct in furtherance of a sale. So marketing that promotes a distribution, in any form, is a trade. Without a receipt or an exemption, it breaches the prospectus requirement. A breach does not need a completed sale.
questions.source_quote: "Accordingly, advertising or marketing activities intended to promote the distribution of securities, in any form, would be prohibited by virtue of the prospectus requirement." — research/sources/csa/cp-41-101-general-prospectus-requirements-companion-policy.txt 41-101CP s.6.3(1), ~L1290-1293

questions.stem: Regulators worry that marketing before a prospectus is available can condition the market. What does conditioning of the market mean?

options.A: Promotion that creates demand before investors have the prospectus
options.B: Price changes that occur after the shares start to trade on an exchange
options.C: An underwriter's purchase of shares to support the offering price
options.D: An issuer's release of factual news that the law requires it to file

questions.rationale: Conditioning of the market means promotion that creates demand before investors have the prospectus. Regulators also worry about equal access to information, tipping and insider trading. Required filings and regular factual news do not promote a distribution, so the prospectus requirement generally does not apply to them.
questions.source_quote: "the overriding concerns implicit and explicit in securities legislation regarding equal access to information, conditioning of the market, tipping and insider trading" — research/sources/csa/cp-41-101-general-prospectus-requirements-companion-policy.txt 41-101CP s.6.2(9), ~L1260-1262

questions.stem: The regulator has issued a receipt for the final prospectus of Ostrova Rail Inc. Its dealer now prepares a newspaper notice about the offering. What legend does NI 41-101 require?

options.A: That no sale can occur until the final receipt is issued
options.B: That the offering is only made by prospectus
options.C: That the regulator has approved the merits of the shares
options.D: That the shares are subject to a four-month restricted period

questions.rationale: After the final receipt, communications carry a legend that the offering is only made by prospectus (s. 13.2). The no-sale legend applies during the waiting period, before the final receipt (s. 13.1). Restricted periods apply to some exempt distributions, not to a prospectus offering.
questions.source_quote: "This offering is only made by prospectus." — research/sources/csa/ni-41-101-general-prospectus-requirements.txt NI 41-101 s.13.2(1), ~L1700

questions.stem: Larchmont Analytics Inc. plans an IPO under a long form prospectus. It has not filed a preliminary prospectus. Which activity can fit a narrow exception to the ban on pre-filing marketing?

options.A: A newspaper ad that states the expected offering price
options.B: A dealer's acceptance of orders that become binding at the final receipt
options.C: Testing of the waters to see if there is enough interest in the IPO
options.D: A standard term sheet sent to the dealer's retail clients

questions.rationale: Before the preliminary prospectus, marketing in furtherance of the distribution is generally banned. NI 41-101 s. 13.4 gives a narrow testing-of-the-waters exception for IPO issuers. Standard term sheets belong to the waiting period, after the preliminary receipt. Ads and order-taking are not allowed.
questions.source_quote: "the prospectus requirement does not apply to a solicitation of an expression of interest in order to ascertain if there would be sufficient interest in an initial public offering of securities by an issuer pursuant to a long form prospectus if" — research/sources/csa/ni-41-101-general-prospectus-requirements.txt NI 41-101 s.13.4(2), ~L1745

questions.stem: A material change occurs in the affairs of Brantmoor Metals Ltd., a reporting issuer, on June 3. No confidential-filing exception applies. What must Brantmoor do?

options.A: File a material change report by June 3, with no news release
options.B: Issue a news release by June 13 and file a report within 30 days
options.C: Disclose the change in its next interim financial report
options.D: Issue a news release immediately and file a report by June 13

questions.rationale: NI 51-102 s. 7.1(1) requires an immediate news release. The issuer must also file a material change report as soon as practicable, and no later than 10 days after the change. So June 13 is the last date. Disclosure in a later financial report is too late.
questions.source_quote: "immediately issue and file a news release authorized by an executive officer disclosing the nature and substance of the change; and (b) as soon as practicable, and in any event within 10 days of the date on which the change occurs, file a Form 51-102F3 Material Change Report" — research/sources/csa/ni-51-102-continuous-disclosure-obligations.txt NI 51-102 s.7.1(1), ~L2488-2494

questions.stem: A dealer distributes four securities under prospectus exemptions. Which security is free trading after the distribution, with no restricted or seasoning period?

options.A: Shares sold to an accredited investor by a reporting issuer
options.B: A bond guaranteed by the government of a province
options.C: Shares of a private issuer sold to a close friend of a founder
options.D: Units sold to a corporation under the minimum amount exemption

questions.rationale: Debt issued or guaranteed by the Government of Canada or a province is exempt because of the security itself. NI 45-106 notes that these securities are free trading. First trades after the accredited investor and minimum amount exemptions have a restricted period. Private issuer securities have a seasoning period.
questions.source_quote: "This provision is not cited in any Appendix of National Instrument 45-102 Resale of Securities.  These securities are free trading." — research/sources/csa/ni-45-106-prospectus-exemptions.txt NI 45-106 note to s.2.34 and s.2.35, ~L2568, ~L2638

questions.stem: An issuer wants to sell commercial paper under the exemption in NI 45-106 s. 2.35. Which commercial paper can qualify?

options.A: Paper that matures in 18 months and has a high credit rating
options.B: Paper that matures in 6 months and has no credit rating
options.C: Paper that matures in 9 months and has a qualifying high rating
options.D: Paper that has no fixed maturity but has a high credit rating

questions.rationale: Under s. 2.35, the paper must mature not more than one year from issue. It must also have a credit rating from a designated rating organization at or above a set category. Paper that matures in 18 months fails the term test. Unrated paper fails the rating test.
questions.source_quote: "the note or commercial paper matures not more than one year from the date of issue;" — research/sources/csa/ni-45-106-prospectus-exemptions.txt NI 45-106 s.2.35(1)(a), ~L2643

questions.stem: Ferrovale Cabinets Ltd. is not a reporting issuer. Its articles restrict share transfers. It has 46 outside shareholders and 12 employee shareholders. Does it meet the ownership limit for a private issuer?

options.A: Yes, because employees do not count toward the limit of 50
options.B: No, because it has 58 shareholders, which is more than 50
options.C: No, because a private issuer cannot have employee shareholders
options.D: Yes, because the limit applies only to holders of debt securities

questions.rationale: A private issuer's securities, other than non-convertible debt, can have no more than 50 beneficial owners. Employees and former employees of the issuer or its affiliates do not count. So only the 46 outside shareholders count. Option B counts the employees, which the rule excludes.
questions.source_quote: "are beneficially owned by not more than 50 persons, not including employees and former employees of the issuer or its affiliates" — research/sources/csa/ni-45-106-prospectus-exemptions.txt NI 45-106 s.2.4(1)(b)(ii), ~L1260-1261

questions.stem: A private issuer counts its beneficial owners. One shareholder is Pellwood Holdings Ltd., which eight people created only to hold the issuer's shares. How many owners does Pellwood count as?

options.A: One, because each corporation counts as one owner
options.B: None, because corporations do not count toward the limit
options.C: One, unless Pellwood owns more than 10% of the shares
options.D: Eight, because each of its owners counts separately

questions.rationale: Each person counts as one beneficial owner. The exception is a person created or used only to buy or hold the issuer's securities. Then each of its beneficial owners counts separately. Pellwood exists only to hold the shares, so it counts as eight. Option A ignores this look-through rule.
questions.source_quote: "each person is counted as one beneficial owner unless the person is created or used solely to purchase or hold securities of the issuer in which case each beneficial owner or each beneficiary of the person, as the case may be, must be counted as a separate beneficial owner" — research/sources/csa/ni-45-106-prospectus-exemptions.txt NI 45-106 s.2.4(1)(b)(ii), ~L1261-1265

questions.stem: Esker Farms Ltd., a private issuer, sells shares to a close friend of its director under the private issuer exemption. The friend is not an accredited investor. The director asks for a finder's fee. Is the fee allowed?

options.A: Yes, if the issuer discloses the fee to the purchaser in writing
options.B: No, because a director cannot get a finder's fee on this distribution
options.C: Yes, because the friend is in a listed category of purchaser
options.D: No, because a close friend cannot buy under this exemption

questions.rationale: Except on a distribution to an accredited investor, no director, officer, founder or control person can get a commission or finder's fee. The friend is not an accredited investor, so the fee is not allowed. A close personal friend of a director is a listed purchaser, so D is wrong.
questions.source_quote: "Except for a distribution to an accredited investor, no commission or finder's fee may be paid to any director, officer, founder or control person of an issuer in connection with a distribution under subsection (2)" — research/sources/csa/ni-45-106-prospectus-exemptions.txt NI 45-106 s.2.4(3), ~L1328-1329

questions.stem: A dealer sells exempt shares to Gideon Rask under the accredited investor exemption. Gideon initials the income category on Form 45-106F9. The dealer asks no questions. Has the dealer met its duty?

options.A: Yes, because the client's initial is a binding representation
options.B: Yes, because the issuer, not the dealer, must check the exemption
options.C: No, because it must take reasonable steps to verify the representation
options.D: No, because only a lawyer can confirm accredited investor status

questions.rationale: The person relying on an exemption must determine that its conditions are met. An initial on Form 45-106F9 is not enough unless the seller has taken reasonable steps to verify it. The dealer relies on the exemption here, so B is wrong. The rules do not require a lawyer.
questions.source_quote: "It will not be sufficient for the seller to accept standard representations in a subscription agreement or an initial beside a category on Form 45-106F9 Form for Individual Accredited Investors unless the seller has taken reasonable steps to verify the representations made by the purchaser." — research/sources/csa/cp-45-106-prospectus-exemptions-companion-policy.txt 45-106CP s.1.9(3), ~L232-234

questions.stem: Leontyne Abara earned $160,000 before tax in each of the last two years. Her spouse earned $170,000 in each year. They expect the same income this year. Does she qualify as an accredited investor under the income test?

options.A: No, because neither spouse alone earned more than $200,000
options.B: Yes, because their combined income exceeds $300,000
options.C: No, because the income test does not combine spouses
options.D: Yes, because her own income exceeds $150,000

questions.rationale: Test (k) needs net income before tax above $200,000 alone, or above $300,000 combined with a spouse. It applies to each of the last two years, with the same level expected this year. Their combined $330,000 exceeds $300,000. Option A ignores the combined limb.
questions.source_quote: "an individual whose net income before taxes exceeded $200 000 in each of the 2 most recent calendar years or whose net income before taxes combined with that of a spouse exceeded $300 000 in each of the 2 most recent calendar years and who, in either case, reasonably expects to exceed that net income level in the current calendar year," — research/sources/csa/ni-45-106-prospectus-exemptions.txt NI 45-106 s.1.1 AI (k), ~L237

questions.stem: Oriel Vantongeren alone owns financial assets of $6,200,000, net of related liabilities. He buys shares under the accredited investor exemption. Which statement about the risk acknowledgement form is correct?

options.A: He must sign Form 45-106F9 at or before the purchase agreement
options.B: He must sign Form 45-106F9 within 30 days after the purchase
options.C: His spouse must also sign Form 45-106F9 with him
options.D: He does not need to sign Form 45-106F9

questions.rationale: His financial assets alone exceed $5,000,000, so he qualifies under test (j.1). An individual under (j.1) does not need Form 45-106F9. Individuals under tests (j), (k) or (l) sign it at or before the purchase agreement. So option A applies to the other tests.
questions.source_quote: "an issuer distributing securities under the accredited investor exemption to an individual who meets the $5 000 000 financial asset test in paragraph (j.1) under the definition of "accredited investor" is not required to obtain a signed risk acknowledgement in Form 45-106F9" — research/sources/csa/cp-45-106-prospectus-exemptions-companion-policy.txt 45-106CP s.3.5(1), ~L774-777

questions.stem: Wendeline Okoro owns $800,000 in securities with no related debt. Her home is worth $4,600,000, with a $200,000 mortgage. She has no other assets or debts. Is she an accredited investor?

options.A: Yes, because her net assets are at least $5,000,000
options.B: No, because her financial assets do not exceed $1,000,000
options.C: No, because the net asset test excludes the personal residence
options.D: Yes, because her financial assets include her home equity

questions.rationale: Test (l) needs net assets of at least $5,000,000. Net assets include the home and its mortgage: $800,000 + $4,600,000 - $200,000 = $5,200,000. She fails test (j), because financial assets exclude the home. But one test is enough, so B is wrong.
questions.source_quote: "the calculation of total assets would include the value of a purchaser's personal residence and the calculation of total liabilities would include the amount of any liability (such as a mortgage) in respect of the purchaser's personal residence." — research/sources/csa/cp-45-106-prospectus-exemptions-companion-policy.txt 45-106CP s.3.5(1), ~L785-788

questions.stem: Ilse Marchand bought shares eight months ago under the accredited investor exemption. The issuer became a reporting issuer two months ago. Can she now resell the shares under NI 45-102 s. 2.5?

options.A: Yes, because four months have passed since the distribution date
options.B: No, because the issuer has not been a reporting issuer for four months
options.C: Yes, because the issuer is now a reporting issuer in Canada
options.D: No, because exempt shares can never be resold to the public

questions.rationale: Section 2.5 needs at least four months from the distribution date. The issuer must also have been a reporting issuer for the four months immediately before the trade. Eight months have passed, but the issuer has been a reporting issuer for only two. So option A misses one condition.
questions.source_quote: "The issuer is and has been a reporting issuer in a jurisdiction of Canada for the four months immediately preceding the trade." — research/sources/csa/ni-45-102-resale-of-securities.txt NI 45-102 s.2.5(2) condition 1, ~L149

questions.stem: Harrowgate Capital Corp. owns 12% of the voting shares of Kestrel Mines Ltd. It offers to buy another 9% from Kestrel's shareholders. How does NI 62-104 treat this offer?

options.A: It is a take-over bid, because the total would be 21% of the class
options.B: It is not a take-over bid, because the offer is for only 9%
options.C: It is a take-over bid only if Harrowgate pays with its own shares
options.D: It is not a take-over bid, because Harrowgate already owns shares

questions.rationale: A take-over bid is an offer for voting or equity securities that, with the offeror's own securities, total 20% or more of the class. Harrowgate's 12% plus 9% equals 21%. Option B ignores the offeror's existing holding. The form of payment does not decide this.
questions.source_quote: "where the securities subject to the offer to acquire, together with the offeror's securities, constitute in the aggregate 20% or more of the outstanding securities of that class of securities at the date of the offer to acquire" — research/sources/csa/ni-62-104-take-over-bids-and-issuer-bids.txt NI 62-104 s.1.1 'take-over bid', ~L244

questions.stem: Three individuals form Sandpiper Ventures Inc. only to buy $150,000 of shares of one issuer under the minimum amount exemption. Sandpiper pays cash and buys as principal. Can the issuer rely on that exemption?

options.A: Yes, because the purchaser is a corporation, not an individual
options.B: Yes, because the purchaser pays at least $150,000 in cash
options.C: No, because the purchaser was created only to use this exemption
options.D: No, because the minimum amount exemption applies only to debt

questions.rationale: The exemption needs a purchaser that is not an individual and pays at least $150,000 in cash for one issuer's securities. But it does not apply to a person created or used only to buy under it. Sandpiper meets the other conditions, so A and B miss this exclusion.
questions.source_quote: "Subsection (1) does not apply to a distribution of a security to a person if the person was created, or is used, solely to purchase or hold securities in reliance on the exemption" — research/sources/csa/ni-45-106-prospectus-exemptions.txt NI 45-106 s.2.10(2), ~L1995-1996

questions.stem: At the annual meeting of a federal corporation, the voting shareholders elect the directors by ordinary resolution. What level of approval does an ordinary resolution need?

options.A: Two thirds of all shares outstanding
options.B: Unanimous approval of the shareholders present
options.C: Two thirds of the votes cast
options.D: A simple majority (50% plus 1) of the votes cast

questions.rationale: Ordinary resolutions need a simple majority, 50 percent plus 1, of the votes cast. Special resolutions, such as for fundamental changes, need two thirds of the votes cast. Approval is measured on votes cast, not on all shares outstanding.
rule_refs: Corporations Canada, Share structure and shareholders
questions.source_quote: "Ordinary resolutions require a simple majority (50 percent plus 1) of votes cast by shareholders." — research/sources/gov/business-structures-corporations-cooperatives-ised.txt ISED Ordinary resolutions, ~L240

questions.stem: A new federal corporation plans two classes of shares. Which share structure meets the minimum rights rule?

options.A: Class A votes; Class B gets dividends and the property left on dissolution
options.B: Class A gets dividends; Class B gets dividends and the property left on dissolution
options.C: Class A votes and gets dividends; Class B votes and gets dividends
options.D: Class A votes; Class B votes and gets the property left on dissolution

questions.rationale: Three rights must exist: to vote, to receive declared dividends and to receive the property left after dissolution. With more than one class, each right must go to at least one class, but no class needs all three. Only option A assigns all three rights.
rule_refs: Corporations Canada, Share structure and shareholders
questions.source_quote: "If there are more than one class of shares, each of the three rights have to be assigned to at least one class of shares, but one class does not need to have all three." — research/sources/gov/business-structures-corporations-cooperatives-ised.txt ISED Share structure, ~L165

questions.stem: Mapleridge Logistics Inc. reports record profits, but its board declares no dividend on the common shares. Linnea Strand, a common shareholder, says the company must pay her a share of the profits. Which statement is correct?

options.A: She has a right to a pro rata share of each year's profits
options.B: She can claim a dividend if profits exceed the prior year's
options.C: She can claim a dividend at the next shareholder meeting
options.D: She has no right to a dividend until the board declares one

questions.rationale: A common shareholder has no right to a dividend until the board declares one. After a declaration, each share of the class gets the same amount, so payment is pro rata. Record profits alone do not create a right to a dividend.
rule_refs: Corporations Canada, Share structure and shareholders
questions.source_quote: "the right to receive dividends (if the board of directors has declared any)" — research/sources/gov/business-structures-corporations-cooperatives-ised.txt ISED Share structure, ~L163

questions.stem: Corvid Media Inc. dissolves. Class A shares carry 10 votes each, and Class B subordinate-voting shares carry one vote each. The articles give both classes equal rights per share on dissolution. What does each Class B share get?

options.A: One tenth of the amount that each Class A share gets
options.B: Nothing, until Class A holders receive their full investment
options.C: The same amount as each Class A share, after creditors and preferred
options.D: Its full issue price, before any payment to the Class A holders

questions.rationale: Common shareholders get what remains after creditors and preferred shareholders. Here the articles give both classes an equal claim per share. Lower voting power does not mean lower economic rights. The difference between the classes is control, so option A confuses votes with value.
rule_refs: Corporations Canada, Share structure and shareholders
questions.source_quote: "If there is more than one class, the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions for each class must also be indicated in the articles." — research/sources/gov/business-structures-corporations-cooperatives-ised.txt ISED Classes of shares, ~L151

questions.stem: Yaretzi Moll holds non-voting common shares of a CBCA corporation. Which statement about her voting rights is correct?

options.A: She can never vote, because her shares are non-voting
options.B: She can vote on certain fundamental issues under the CBCA
options.C: She can vote in director elections if she holds over 10%
options.D: She can vote only after the company misses a dividend

questions.rationale: The CBCA gives holders of non-voting shares the right to attend certain meetings and vote on certain fundamental issues. So option A overstates the restriction. NI 41-101 also defines a non-voting security as one with no general vote, except a vote that law mandates in special cases.
rule_refs: Corporations Canada, Share structure and shareholders
questions.source_quote: "The Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) gives holders of non-voting shares the right to attend certain meetings and vote on certain fundamental issues." — research/sources/gov/business-structures-corporations-cooperatives-ised.txt ISED Shareholders' meetings, ~L258

questions.stem: A bidder offers a large premium for the multiple-voting shares of Tarnby Foods Inc. It makes no offer for the subordinate-voting shares. Which provision lets the subordinate-voting holders take part in the bid?

options.A: A coattail provision
options.B: A cumulative dividend provision
options.C: A retraction provision
options.D: A pre-emptive right provision

questions.rationale: A coattail provision lets the inferior class convert or join a bid made only for the superior-voting class. Without it, a buyer could pay a control premium to the superior class only. Cumulative and retraction features belong to preferred shares and do not deal with take-over bids.

questions.stem: At Brisa Wind Corp., founders hold shares with 10 votes each. Public holders own a second class with one vote each, but that class receives twice the dividend per share. What is the founders' class under NI 41-101?

options.A: Not restricted, because it carries the most votes per share
options.B: Subordinate voting securities, because it gets a smaller dividend
options.C: Non-voting securities, because the other class has greater economic rights
options.D: Restricted securities, because the other class has a greater right to earnings per share

questions.rationale: An equity security is restricted if another class can share in earnings or assets to a greater extent per security (limb (c)). The public class gets twice the dividend, so the founders' class is restricted. Multiple votes alone do not prevent this. The public class is also restricted, because it has fewer votes.
questions.source_quote: "the issuer has issued another class of equity securities that entitle the owners of securities of that other class to participate in the earnings or assets of the issuer to a greater extent, on a per security basis, than the owners of the first class of equity securities" — research/sources/csa/ni-41-101-general-prospectus-requirements.txt NI 41-101 s.1.1 'restricted security' (c), ~L727

questions.stem: Each common share of Norrland Telecom Inc. carries one vote. But no single holder may vote more than 10% of the class. Which NI 41-101 term describes these shares?

options.A: Subordinate voting security
options.B: Restricted voting security
options.C: Non-voting security
options.D: Multiple voting security

questions.rationale: A restricted voting security carries a vote, but with a limit. The limit is on the number or percentage of shares that a person may vote or own. A subordinate voting security has fewer votes per share than another class. The 10% cap makes option B correct.
questions.source_quote: ""restricted voting security" means a restricted security that carries a right to vote subject to a restriction on the number or percentage of securities that may be voted or owned by one or more persons or companies," — research/sources/csa/ni-41-101-general-prospectus-requirements.txt NI 41-101 s.1.1 'restricted voting security', ~L769

questions.stem: Tomasz Wierzbicki notices that the CDR ratio on his hedged CDR has changed since he bought it. The company has made no corporate action. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: The Canadian exchange changed the CDR's trading currency to USD
options.B: The underlying company paid a dividend in U.S. dollars
options.C: Tomasz bought more CDRs in his account
options.D: The USD/CAD exchange rate changed, and the ratio adjusts as part of the hedge

questions.rationale: The CDR ratio changes when the exchange rate changes. This is how the notional currency hedge works, so the ratio is not fixed. Dividends go to holders in CAD and do not explain the change. A holder's own purchases do not change the ratio.

questions.stem: Priya Lachance holds a hedged CDR. Over a month, the underlying share rises 8% in U.S. dollars, and the U.S. dollar falls 4% against the Canadian dollar. About how much does her CDR change?

options.A: About +4%, because the weaker U.S. dollar reduces the gain
options.B: About +12%, because the currency change adds to the gain
options.C: About +8%, less the hedge cost
options.D: About 0%, because the hedge removes the share's return

questions.rationale: A hedged CDR's C$ value changes about as much as the share's return in its home currency. So the USD/CAD change has little effect. The CDR return is about the share's 8% gain, less the hedge cost. Option A describes an unhedged position.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 3.3 currency hedge and CDR ratio

questions.stem: Anders Quayle buys CDRs on a U.S. company. Which statement describes who holds the underlying shares?

options.A: Anders holds them and becomes a registered shareholder
options.B: The U.S. company holds them in trust until Anders sells
options.C: A Canadian financial institution holds them as depositary
options.D: The Canadian exchange holds them for all CDR holders

questions.rationale: A Canadian financial institution acts as depositary and holds the underlying shares. The CDR holder is not a registered shareholder of the foreign company. The holder's rights come through the depositary, under the CDR terms.

questions.stem: A U.S. company's shares trade at a high price. Why does the CDR on this company use a ratio of many CDRs per share?

options.A: To make the CDR return higher than the share's return
options.B: To give each CDR holder more votes than a direct holder
options.C: To remove the hedge cost from the CDR price
options.D: To give each CDR an affordable price in Canadian dollars

questions.rationale: The CDR ratio shows how much of one share each CDR represents. It aims to give each CDR an affordable price. It does not raise the return, because the CDR's percentage change is about the share's home-currency return, less the hedge cost.

questions.stem: The U.S. company behind Margit Solberg's CDRs pays a quarterly dividend. Which statement describes what she receives?

options.A: Additional CDRs instead of cash, under the CDR ratio
options.B: The full dividend on one share for each CDR, paid in USD
options.C: No dividend, because the depositary keeps all dividends
options.D: Her share of the dividend, in proportion to her CDRs, paid in CAD

questions.rationale: A CDR holder gets the price changes of the underlying share and its dividends, paid in CAD. Each CDR is a fraction of a share, so she gets a proportional amount, not the full dividend per CDR. The depositary passes the dividends through under the CDR terms.

questions.stem: Two retailers have the same sales and operating profit. Hollin Stores Ltd. has no debt. Dunmore Retail Inc. has heavy debt. Operating profit at both falls 15%. Which outcome is most likely?

options.A: Both companies' profit for shareholders falls by about 15%
options.B: Hollin's profit for shareholders falls more, because it has no debt
options.C: Dunmore's profit for shareholders falls more, because interest stays the same
options.D: Dunmore's profit for shareholders falls less, because its interest is deductible

questions.rationale: Interest payments do not change when operating profit falls. So heavy debt makes the profit for shareholders change more. This is financial (leverage) risk. Dunmore still pays its full interest, so its shareholders absorb a larger percentage drop. Hollin's drop stays close to 15%.

questions.stem: Rhiannon Asante holds 40 stocks across many sectors. In a broad market sell-off, most of her stocks fall at the same time. She asks why diversification did not protect her. Which answer is correct?

options.A: Her stocks share company-specific risk, which needs more stocks to remove
options.B: Market risk affects most shares at once, and diversification cannot remove it
options.C: Forty stocks are too few to reduce any kind of risk
options.D: Her stocks lack liquidity, so they all fell together

questions.rationale: Market (systematic) risk affects most shares at the same time. Diversification cannot remove it. Diversification can reduce company-specific risk, which 40 stocks across sectors largely do. So option A names the wrong risk.

questions.stem: Callum Ferreira owns shares of a Canadian exporter that earns most of its revenue in U.S. dollars. He says CAD-priced shares carry no currency risk. The Canadian dollar then strengthens. What is the most likely effect?

options.A: No effect, because the shares trade in Canadian dollars
options.B: Higher profit, because the stronger CAD buys more U.S. goods
options.C: Lower profit and share price, because its U.S. revenue is worth fewer CAD
options.D: No effect, because only unhedged CDRs carry currency risk

questions.rationale: Shares priced in CAD have no direct currency risk. But a company with foreign revenue has indirect currency risk. A stronger CAD reduces the CAD value of the exporter's U.S. revenue, so its profit and share price can fall. Option A ignores indirect risk.

questions.stem: Dagny Holm compares two ways to own a U.S. company: buy its shares directly in USD or buy its hedged CDR in Canada. Which cost applies to the direct purchase but not to the CDR?

options.A: A commission on the trade
options.B: A bid-ask spread on the trade
options.C: A hedge cost built into the price
options.D: A currency-conversion spread

questions.rationale: A direct purchase of foreign shares adds a currency-conversion spread. The CDR trades in CAD, so it has no conversion spread. But its price includes a hedge cost, so option C applies to the CDR. Both choices carry commissions and bid-ask spreads.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 3.4 costs of acquiring and holding

questions.stem: Soren Vik wants a CDR on a large U.S. company. The CDR trades a few thousand units a day, but the underlying share trades millions. Which risk is greater for the CDR than for the underlying share?

options.A: Liquidity risk, with possibly wider bid-ask spreads
options.B: Business risk, because CDR issuers earn less profit
options.C: Market risk, because CDRs trade on a smaller exchange
options.D: Currency risk, because the CDR is priced in CAD

questions.rationale: Thin trading means wide spreads. A depositary receipt's volume may be below the underlying share's volume, so liquidity risk can be higher. Business and market risks are the same as for the underlying company. A hedged CDR mostly removes currency risk, so option D is wrong.

questions.stem: Imogen Barlow paid $5,000 for common shares of Fairhaven Bakeries Ltd. The company fails and owes its creditors far more than its assets. What is the most Imogen can lose?

options.A: $5,000, because her liability is limited to what she paid
options.B: Her share of the unpaid debts, in proportion to her shares
options.C: $5,000 plus any dividends she received in the last year
options.D: An unlimited amount, because common shareholders rank last

questions.rationale: Shareholders' liability is limited to the amount they paid for their shares. They are usually not liable for the corporation's debts. Imogen ranks last and can lose the whole $5,000. But ranking last does not make her liable for more than she invested.
rule_refs: Corporations Canada, Share structure and shareholders
questions.source_quote: "The shareholders' liability in a corporation is limited to the amount they paid for their shares; shareholders are usually not liable for the corporation's debts." — research/sources/gov/business-structures-corporations-cooperatives-ised.txt ISED Rights and responsibilities, ~L222

questions.stem: The founders of Ostler Ceramics Inc. own all its shares and want to keep control. The company needs new capital. Which disadvantage of issuing new common shares matters most to them?

options.A: New shares create a fixed payment that can cause a default
options.B: New shares dilute the founders' control and EPS
options.C: New shares must be repaid at a set maturity date
options.D: New shares raise the company's debt-to-equity ratio

questions.rationale: New common shares spread earnings and votes over more shares. So the founders lose part of their control and EPS. Common shares have no fixed payment and no maturity, so A and C describe debt. New equity lowers debt-to-equity.

questions.stem: The CFO of Thornfield Software Ltd. says common equity is free capital, because the company need not pay dividends. Which response best corrects this view?

options.A: Equity costs more than debt, because shareholders demand higher returns
options.B: Equity is free, but only until the company first declares a dividend
options.C: Equity costs less than debt, because dividends are tax-deductible
options.D: Equity costs the same as debt, because both appear on the balance sheet

questions.rationale: The company has no obligation to pay dividends, but equity is not free. Investors demand higher returns on common shares, so equity costs more than debt. Dividends come out of after-tax profit, whereas interest is generally deductible. So option C reverses the tax treatment.

questions.stem: Jasper Nwosu holds common shares, bonds and preferred shares of Halcyon Grain Corp. Over five years, Halcyon's profits triple. Which security most likely gains most from this growth?

options.A: The bonds, because their interest has priority
options.B: The preferred shares, because their dividends are fixed
options.C: The bonds, because their price rises with profits
options.D: The common shares, because they get all profit above the fixed claims

questions.rationale: Creditors and preferred shareholders get fixed amounts. Common shareholders get everything above that, so their possible gain has no limit. Fixed interest and fixed preferred dividends do not rise when profits triple. Priority protects the bonds in a failure, but it does not add to their return.

questions.stem: Marlow Freight Ltd. wants a new bank loan. The bank will lend only if Marlow first lowers its debt-to-equity ratio. Which action best meets this condition?

options.A: Issue new bonds and use the cash to buy equipment
options.B: Issue new common shares and use the cash to repay some debt
options.C: Pay a large special dividend to the common shareholders
options.D: Buy back common shares with cash on hand

questions.rationale: An issue of common shares strengthens the balance sheet and lowers debt-to-equity. Using the cash to repay debt lowers the ratio further. New bonds add debt. A special dividend or a buyback reduces equity, so each raises the ratio.
